parts.name: Calf / Achilles
parts.pubmed: (achilles tendinopathy OR calf strain) AND (exercise OR rehabilitation OR loading)
parts.summary: Tendon and calf problems respond best to gradually heavier calf loading, not rest. You can usually keep running if pain stays at 5/10 or less during the run and is back to normal by the next morning.
parts.run_rule: Pain-monitoring rule: keep running if pain is 5/10 or less during and after, and settles by next morning. Otherwise cut the run or swap for the bike.

exercises.name: Calf raise hold
steps: Stand on both feet, rise halfway onto your toes.
Hold still. Mild discomfort (up to 3/10) is fine.
Rest 1–2 min between holds.
exercises.mediaTitle: NHS inform: calf and ankle exercises

exercises.name: Heel raises (straight knee)
exercises.dose: 3 × 15, daily; progress two feet → one foot → with a backpack
steps: Stand on a step edge holding a rail.
Rise up on both feet, lower slowly over 3 s.
Progress to one foot when 3 × 15 feels easy.
exercises.mediaTitle: NHS inform: calf and ankle exercises

exercises.name: Bent-knee heel raises (soleus)
steps: Same as heel raises but with knees bent about 30°.
Keep the knee bend constant the whole time.
exercises.mediaTitle: NHS inform: calf and ankle exercises

exercises.name: Eccentric heel drops (Alfredson)
exercises.dose: 3 × 15 straight knee + 3 × 15 bent knee, twice a day for 12 weeks
steps: Rise up on both feet on a step.
Shift to the sore leg and lower the heel below the step over 3 s.
Use the good leg to get back up.
exercises.mediaTitle: NHS inform: calf and ankle exercises

exercises.name: Heavy loaded calf raise
steps: Seated or standing calf machine, or a barbell/dumbbells.
3 s up, 3 s down, full range.
Add weight when 8 reps feel easy.
exercises.mediaTitle: NHS inform: calf and ankle exercises

parts.name: Shin
parts.pubmed: (medial tibial stress syndrome OR shin splints OR tibial bone stress injury) AND (treatment OR rehabilitation)
parts.summary: Shin pain along the inner edge is usually medial tibial stress syndrome. The research on treatments is weak, so the plan is load management: fewer and easier miles, then a gradual walk-run return. Pain in one small spot on the bone that hurts to press, or pain when walking, may be a bone stress injury and needs a doctor.
parts.run_rule: Cut weekly miles, run on softer surfaces, and use walk-run intervals. Increase distance before speed. A slightly quicker cadence lowers bone load.
parts.redflag: Pain in one spot on the bone that hurts to press, pain when walking, or pain at night: stop running and see a doctor to rule out a stress fracture.

exercises.name: Heel raises (straight and bent knee)
steps: Stand on a step holding a rail.
Rise up, lower slowly over 3 s.
Do half with knees straight and half slightly bent.
exercises.mediaTitle: NHS inform: calf and ankle exercises

exercises.name: Walk-run return
exercises.dose: e.g. 5 × (1 min run + 1 min walk), every other day; add 1 min run per session if pain-free
steps: Only start once walking is pain-free and the bone isn't tender to press.
Progress distance before speed.

parts.name: Knee (front / kneecap)
parts.summary: Pain around or behind the kneecap. Exercise is the main treatment, and combining hip and knee strengthening works better than knee exercises alone.
parts.run_rule: Change your load rather than stopping completely. A common guide is to keep pain mild (about 3/10 or less) and not worse the next day. Flat routes help; hills and downhill running usually aggravate it.

exercises.name: Side-lying leg raise (hip abduction)
steps: Lie on your side, bottom knee bent.
Lift the top leg slightly behind you, toes pointing forward.
Lower slowly.
exercises.mediaTitle: NHS inform: patellofemoral knee pain exercises

exercises.name: Wall sit (shallow)
steps: Back against a wall, slide down to a comfortable bend (not deeper than 60°).
Hold. Pain up to 3/10 is OK.
exercises.mediaTitle: NHS inform: patellofemoral knee pain exercises

exercises.name: Glute bridge
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent.
Squeeze glutes and lift hips, hold 2 s, lower.
exercises.mediaTitle: NHS inform: patellofemoral knee pain exercises

exercises.name: Step-down
steps: Stand on a low step on the sore leg.
Slowly lower the other heel to the floor, knee tracking over your middle toe.
Push back up.
exercises.mediaTitle: NHS inform: patellofemoral knee pain exercises

exercises.name: Loaded squat / split squat
steps: Squat to a depth that is comfortable, adding depth then load over weeks.
exercises.mediaTitle: NHS inform: patellofemoral knee pain exercises

parts.name: Outside of knee / IT band
parts.pubmed: iliotibial band syndrome AND (runners OR running) AND (treatment OR exercise)
parts.summary: Pain on the outside of the knee, often after a set distance into a run. The best-supported treatment is hip abductor strengthening.
parts.run_rule: Shorten runs to below the point where pain starts. Avoid downhills and running on cambered roads for a while.

exercises.name: Side-lying hip abduction
steps: Lie on your side, bottom knee bent.
Lift the top leg up and slightly back, toes forward.
Lower over 2 s.

exercises.name: Side plank
steps: On your elbow and the side of your knees (easier) or feet (harder).
Keep hips lifted in a straight line.

exercises.name: Lateral band walk
steps: Band around ankles or above knees, half squat.
Step sideways without letting the knees fall in.

exercises.name: Single-leg squat to box
steps: Stand on one leg in front of a box or bench.
Sit back to touch it, keeping the knee in line with your toes.

parts.name: Hamstring
parts.pubmed: hamstring (strain OR injury) AND (rehabilitation OR exercise) AND (running OR runners)
parts.summary: Tightness or pain at the back of the thigh. Start with holds, then build strength. In a trial, a rehab programme built on lengthening exercises got players back about three weeks sooner than conventional exercises. Nordic curls are strongly supported for preventing hamstring injuries once you're pain-free.
parts.run_rule: Keep runs easy and avoid strides or fast work until bridges and leg curls are pain-free.

exercises.name: Bridge hold
steps: Lie on your back, heels on the floor, knees bent about 90°.
Lift hips and hold.

exercises.name: Single-leg bridge
steps: As a bridge, but with one foot lifted.
Keep the hips level.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
steps: Dumbbells or barbell, slight knee bend.
Hinge at the hips until you feel the hamstrings stretch, then stand up.

exercises.name: Nordic hamstring curl
steps: Kneel with ankles held down.
Lower your body forward as slowly as you can, catch yourself with your hands.
Push back up.

parts.name: Hip / glute
parts.pubmed: (gluteal tendinopathy OR greater trochanteric pain syndrome OR hip pain) AND (runners OR exercise)
parts.summary: Pain on the outside of the hip or in the glute, often gluteal tendinopathy. In a trial, load-management advice plus hip strengthening beat both a steroid injection and waiting. Avoid positions that compress the side of the hip, like crossing your legs or lying on that side.
parts.run_rule: Run on flat routes with a slightly shorter stride. Ease off if pain lingers into the next day.

exercises.name: Standing hip abduction hold
steps: Stand side-on to a wall, press the outside of the leg nearest the wall into it.
Hold without hitching your hip.
exercises.mediaTitle: NHS inform: greater trochanteric pain exercises

exercises.name: Glute bridge
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, lift hips, hold 2 s.
exercises.mediaTitle: NHS inform: greater trochanteric pain exercises

exercises.name: Side plank
steps: On your elbow and knees or feet, hips lifted.

parts.name: Foot / heel
parts.pubmed: plantar fasciitis OR plantar heel pain AND (exercise OR strength training)
parts.summary: Heel pain that is worst with the first steps in the morning is usually plantar fasciitis. Heavy, slow heel raises with the toes lifted beat stretching alone at 3 months.
parts.run_rule: Keep runs short and on soft surfaces while it's sore. Supportive shoes or inserts help day to day.

exercises.name: Heel raise with towel under toes
exercises.dose: Every other day: 3 × 12 (weeks 1–2), then 4 × 10 with a backpack, then 5 × 8 heavier
steps: Stand on one foot on a step, rolled towel under your toes.
3 s up, 2 s pause at the top, 3 s down.
Add weight in a backpack as it gets easy.

exercises.name: Calf and plantar fascia stretch
exercises.dose: 3 × 30 s, a few times a day
steps: Before getting up, pull your toes back toward your shin with one hand.
Hold until you feel the stretch along the arch.

parts.name: Lower back
parts.pubmed: low back pain AND exercise therapy AND (systematic review OR randomized)
parts.summary: Most low back pain settles with movement. Exercise helps pain, and no single type is clearly best, so pick ones you'll keep doing.
parts.run_rule: Easy running and walking are fine if pain doesn't get worse. Leg numbness, weakness, or problems with bladder or bowel need urgent care.
parts.redflag: Numbness in the groin, leg weakness, or new bladder or bowel problems: get urgent medical care.

exercises.name: Cat–camel
steps: On hands and knees, round your back, then let it dip gently.

exercises.name: Bird dog
steps: On hands and knees, reach one arm and the opposite leg out.
Hold 3 s without the hips twisting.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, lift hips, hold 2 s.

exercises.name: Side plank
steps: On your elbow and knees or feet, hips lifted.

parts.name: General soreness
parts.pubmed: (delayed onset muscle soreness OR exercise-induced muscle damage) AND recovery
parts.summary: Normal post-training soreness. Massage is the best-supported option for soreness and fatigue. Compression, active recovery, cold water and cryotherapy help a little too.
parts.run_rule: Run easy or take a rest day. Soreness that is sharp, in one spot, or still getting worse after 3 days is not normal soreness, so log it as Pain.

exercises.name: Easy active recovery
exercises.dose: 20–30 min very easy bike, walk or swim
steps: Conversational effort, heart rate well below your easy-run range.

exercises.name: Massage or foam rolling
steps: Slow passes over the sore muscles, moderate pressure.

exercises.name: Cold water immersion
steps: Skip it after strength sessions if you're trying to build muscle.

exercises.name: Compression garments
exercises.dose: Wear for a few hours after long runs
steps: Calf sleeves or tights.

disclaimer: General, research-based guidance, not a diagnosis. See a physiotherapist or doctor if pain is severe, getting worse, or not improving after 2 weeks.
